name: Air-to-starch reactor
effect: life's molecules can be made from non-living chemicals
how: Carbon dioxide from the air is combined with hydrogen to make a simple alcohol, which is purified and fed through a chain of chemical and enzyme steps that build it up into starch, the main food in grain. No plant, soil or field is involved. Such a plant could grow staple food in a building, far faster per acre than wheat.
why: Food grown with no plants at all, a direct heir of Wöhler's urea.
